Class BraidedMonoidal := { braided_is_monoidal : @Monoidal C; braid {x y} : x (x) y ~> y (x) x; braid_natural : natural (@braid); hexagon_identity {x y z} : tensor_assoc o braid o tensor_assoc << (x(x)y)(x)z ~~> y(x)(z(x)x) >> id (x) braid o tensor_assoc o braid (x) id; hexagon_identity_sym {...} : ... }.

statement_record.book: A monoidal category B is symmetric when equipped with natural isomorphisms gamma_{a,b} : a(x)b ~= b(x)a satisfying (1) gamma_{b,a} o gamma_{a,b} = 1, (2) the unit compatibility rho_b = lambda_b o gamma_{b,e}, and (3) the hexagon coherence with the associator.
statement_record.intree: SymmetricMonoidal = BraidedMonoidal (a natural iso braid : x(x)y ~> y(x)x with braid_natural and the two hexagon_identity / hexagon_identity_sym laws) together with braid_invol : braid o braid ~ id.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. The in-tree class follows the modern Joyal-Street/nLab axiomatization (braided base + involution). Mac Lane's condition (1) gamma o gamma = 1 IS braid_invol; his hexagon (3) is hexagon_identity (the braided base even supplies BOTH hexagons, redundantly equivalent under braid_invol, per the file's hexagon_rotated lemma). Mac Lane's separate unit-braiding axiom (2) rho_b = lambda_b o gamma_{b,e} is not stated as a field because it is derivable from the hexagons+triangle+pentagon in any braided monoidal category (standard; the same fact is noted at Structure/Monoidal/Heunen_Vicary.v:58 as 'derivable from Mac Lane's coherence theorem'). evidence.intree_statement: Class Enriched (K : Category) `{@Monoidal K} := { eobj : Type; ehom : eobj -> eobj -> K where "a |-> b" := (ehom a b); eid {x} : I ~{K}~> (x |-> x); ecompose {x y z} : (y|->z) (x) (x|->y) ~{K}~> (x|->z); eid_left {x y} : ecompose o eid (x) id << I (x) (x|->y) ~~> (x|->y) >> unit_left; eid_right {x y} : ecompose o id (x) eid << (x|->y)(x)I ~~> (x|->y) >> unit_right; ecompose_assoc {x y z w} : ecompose o ecompose (x) id << ... >> ecompose o id (x) ecompose o tensor_assoc }.

Theorem Category_is_Enriched_over_Set : Enriched Sets <-> Category. (both directions Defined) -- the underlying ordinary category obtained by the base's Set-valued hom, exactly Mac Lane's U R via U = B(e,-).

statement_record.book: Relative to a monoidal category B, a B-category (V-category, category enriched over B) consists of a set R of objects, a hom-object R(r,s) in B for each pair, composition arrows R(s,t)(x)R(r,s) -> R(r,t), unit arrows e -> R(r,r), subject to the usual associativity and unit axioms. Applying a functor U : B -> Set (e.g. U = B(e,-)) to the hom-objects yields an ordinary underlying category U R.
statement_record.intree: Class Enriched (K){@Monoidal K}: objects eobj : Type, hom-object ehom : eobj->eobj->K, identity eid : I ~> (x|->x), composition ecompose : (y|->z)(x)(x|->y) ~> (x|->z), with eid_left, eid_right (unit axioms) and ecompose_assoc (associativity). Category_is_Enriched_over_Set gives the K=Set underlying-category correspondence in both directions.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Field-for-field match to Mac Lane's B-category: eobj = the object-set R (rendered as a Type, the setoid-library convention), ehom = R(r,s) in B, ecompose = composition R(s,t)(x)R(r,s)->R(r,t) (codomain factor on the left, as Mac Lane writes it), eid = unit e->R(r,r), and the three coherence fields = the associativity + two unit axioms. Base is bare Monoidal K, precisely the level Mac Lane states the definition at ('this has only hom-objects... The full theory works when B is closed, not merely monoidal'). Mac Lane's underlying-category-via-U remark is realized by Category_is_Enriched_over_Set (the U = Set case, the cleanest instance).
